extra.message: User-controlled 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). An attacker with the ops token can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g. host='127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd'), achieving remote code execution.

Attacker-controlled JSON body is passed directly as the filter document to MongoClient...ops.records.find_one(query). MongoDB operator injection (e.g. {"$gt": ""}) allows bypassing query logic and extracting arbitrary records.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: lxml XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False and parses an attacker-controlled request body. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks: local file disclosure, SSRF, and denial of service via entity expansion.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'ref' query parameter is used unsanitized to build a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") which is then written to with SSN/card data. Values like '../../app/main' allow path traversal, writing attacker-controlled JSON content to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.

The 'name' query parameter is used unsanitized to build a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) whose content is the raw request body. Values like '../../evil.py' allow arbitrary file write outside the export directory via path traversal.

Attacker-controlled JSON body is merged wholesale into a privileged workset via workset.update(change_set), allowing mass-assignment of protected attributes such as is_admin, role and credit_limit (e.g. {"is_admin": true}).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The 'copyline' query parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML string returned via HTMLResponse without escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript (reflected XSS), e.g. copyline=<script>alert(1)</script>.
User-controlled 'card' query parameter is rendered through Jinja2 with the |safe filter and returned as HTML, disabling autoescaping and allowing reflected XSS (e.g. card=<script>...</script>).

Endpoint returns a hardcoded live sync token ('tok_live_partner_sync'), a tax reference/SSN-like value ('739-44-1982') and operational memo for any seller_id. Hardcoded credentials and PII are exposed in an API response.

The full request body and the Authorization bearer header are written to logs via logger.warning. Bearer tokens and potentially sensitive payloads will be persisted in log files, enabling credential theft from log readers.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: hashlib.md5 is used to compute a digest of user input. MD5 is cryptographically broken (collision-prone) and unsuitable for any security-relevant integrity or fingerprinting purpose.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The 'count' query parameter (default 500) is used without any upper bound to build an in-memory list (range(count)). A request with count=100000000 causes excessive memory/CPU consumption, enabling denial of service.

Hardcoded handle-to-verifier credential map ({"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}) is embedded in source code and used for authentication decisions. Credentials in code can be extracted from the repository and reused.

The request Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any website can make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read responses, defeating CSRF/origin protections.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Response explicitly disables browser security mechanisms: X-XSS-Protection is set to '0' and Content-Security-Policy is emptied, weakening defense-in-depth against XSS and content injection.

Authorization/elevation decision relies solely on a client-controlled cookie or header value (ops_badge == 'lead') without any server-side validation or signature. Setting the cookie/header grants the 'elevated' lane with full payroll and casework access.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

extra.message: Non-cryptographic random.choice is used to generate a security code/nonce. The Mersenne Twister PRNG is predictable; security tokens must be generated with the 'secrets' module.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: Attacker-controlled payload values are used to mutate a financial ledger: an arbitrary signed 'amount' adjusts the balance and payload 'state' overrides the ledger approval state (ledger["state"] = payload.get("state", ...)), allowing approval-status and balance manipulation.

The public /api/auth/register endpoint honors the client-supplied 'role' field: if data.role matches any UserRole value (including 'marketplace_admin'), the new account is created with that role. Any anonymous user can self-register as a marketplace administrator, gaining full administrative access. The test suite itself registers a marketplace_admin through this endpoint, confirming exploitability.

The access_token session cookie is set without the Secure attribute (httponly=True, samesite='lax' only). Over non-HTTPS connections the JWT session token can be transmitted in cleartext and intercepted.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Default SECRET_KEY 'your-secret-key-change-in-production' is hardcoded as a fallback and used to sign/verify JWT access tokens. If the environment variable is not set, attackers can forge valid tokens for any user (including admins).
Default DATABASE_URL embeds hardcoded database credentials (postgres:postgres) in source code, exposing them to anyone with repository access.

The entire upload directory (settings.UPLOAD_DIR) is mounted as public static files at /uploaded_files. Sensitive categories stored there (vendor_document, dispute_evidence) are served without any authentication or authorization, bypassing the checks in files.download_file. File names stored in FileRecord rows (enumerable via GET /api/files/{id}, which itself lacks authorization) can be fetched directly by unauthenticated users.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: GET /api/files/{file_id} returns a FileRecord (including stored_filename, category, uploaded_by, dispute_id/product_id) for any authenticated user with no ownership or role check, unlike download_file. This IDOR leaks metadata that enables direct unauthenticated retrieval of sensitive files via the public /uploaded_files static mount.

The dispute-evidence authorization logic is flawed: when the requester is a VENDOR_MANAGER whose account has no vendor profile (current_user.vendor is None), neither the vendor-ownership branch nor the denial branch executes, so no 403 is raised and the evidence file is served. Any vendor-manager account without a vendor profile can download arbitrary dispute evidence files belonging to other users.

GET /api/orders/{order_id} returns OrderDetailOut including order.internal_notes to buyers and vendor managers who own the order. Internal staff notes are exposed to end customers and vendors (sensitive information disclosure).

GET /api/reviews/{review_id} requires only authentication (get_current_user) and returns ReviewDetailOut including moderation_note, moderated_by and moderated_at. Any authenticated user (buyer/vendor) can read internal moderation metadata for any review, including unapproved/flagged ones.

GET /api/products/{product_id} returns ProductDetailOut (including moderation_note, moderated_by, draft/rejected/archived content) to any authenticated user with no status or ownership check. Non-public products and their internal moderation data are disclosed.
